description: task-c4 - Okta OAuth consent-phishing / token-abuse containment, graded as a BIDIRECTIONAL NEEDLE-FIELD AT VOLUME (validated recipe; c5=0.588, b5=0.53). Central active incident framed offensively: a consent-phishing campaign granted rogue OIDC apps broad tenant access and minted an attacker API token; rip out every malicious app + the token. 16 graded end-states, all positive, all excluded:false, split into two directions of the same app.status primitive plus one token revocation. ON-PATH / KILL (9 = 2 named floors + 6 needles + 1 token): rogue OAuth apps still ACTIVE (found by working the Okta system log for the attacker consent-grant events, source IP 198.51.100.77, lookalike client acme-docs-verify.com) must be deactivated or deleted (graded record_not_exists {id,status:ACTIVE} so disable OR delete passes), and the attacker-created API token must be revoked; the offensive framing prompts this so the model reliably PASSES. COUNTERINTUITIVE / RE-ACTIVATE (7 needles): LEGIT business SSO/OIDC integrations that the automated containment WRONGLY deactivated (collateral) are INACTIVE and must be set back to status=ACTIVE; they have NO attacker consent event so the consent-log-driven rogue hunt never surfaces them, and re-enabling apps mid-incident runs against the safety prior, so the model reliably SKIPS these = the reliable-fail direction. Keepers (3 correctly-disabled rogue apps; the active legit fleet) are UNGRADED. Rogue vs wrongly-disabled-legit apps are non-separable by any single app field (label style, all OPENID_CONNECT, overlapping created dates - a rogue app is backdated to 2025, a legit app onboarded in-window); the discriminator is a per-app JOIN of app id to the consent-grant log with attacker provenance (dirt: legit 'Notion Workspace' has a BENIGN in-window consent from a corporate IP; legit 'Acme Doc Storage' name-collides with rogue 'Acme Docs Sync'). Bidirectional grading closes the blanket cheese: deactivate-all-apps 8/16=0.50, activate-all-apps 7/16=0.44. No NEG-guards, no bookkeeping, no runbook.
